title: The giant on the cover of Hobbes’s Leviathan is made of more than 300 tiny people

cover.alt: The 1651 engraved title page of Leviathan: a crowned giant, its body made of crowds of tiny people, rises over hills and a town holding a sword and a bishop’s crosier, above panels of symbols around the title.

body: Thomas Hobbes published *Leviathan* in 1651, arguing that people should hand power to a single absolute sovereign through a social contract. Its famous title page, etched by the Parisian Abraham Bosse after long discussions with Hobbes, makes the argument in one picture. The crowned giant’s torso and arms are built from over three hundred people, all facing away from us, so the ruler literally is the state made of its subjects. In his hands he holds a sword and a bishop’s crosier, uniting earthly and church power in one sovereign.

slides.label: people make up the giant’s torso and arms
slides.text: All of them face away from the viewer. Only the giant’s own head has a visible face.

steps.label: Without government: a war of all against all
Life is nasty, brutish and short
People agree to a social contract
An undivided sovereign keeps the peace

slides.text: And the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
slides.attribution: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan (1651), on life without a state

slides.heading: Match each earthly power to its church twin
slides.explanation: The panels below the giant pair them off: earthly power on the left under the sword, the church’s power on the right under the crosier.

slides.alt: Oil portrait of Thomas Hobbes as an old man, with long white hair, a grey moustache and a wide white collar against a dark background.
slides.caption: Thomas Hobbes, painted by John Michael Wright.

slides.question: The Latin line across the top of the page is from the Book of Job. What does it say?
options: No power on earth compares to him
The meek shall inherit the earth
Man is a wolf to man
slides.explanation: ‘Non est potestas Super Terram quae Comparetur ei’: there is no power on earth to be compared to him.
